sections.h2: Which Warren County offices handle a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Two offices in the Warren County Administration Building at 101 Mockingbird Lane in Warrenton split the work. Kathryn Smith is the Assessor, in Suite 202, reachable at 636-456-8885 extension 1227. Her office sets the value of land and buildings. Julie Schaumberg is the Collector, in Suite 200, at 636-456-3330, and her office sends the bills and takes the money.

The Collector's office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and answers email at collector@warrencountymo.gov. It states that it cannot add to or change a tax statement unless the Assessor makes the change first. A valuation question therefore goes to the Assessor, and a payment question goes to the Collector.

The Collector's site also carries a 2026 tax rate PDF, a table comparing 2025 and 2026 rates, a tax sale list and a holiday calendar. The Assessor's site offers parcel and personal property searches, and it says emailed assessment forms are not accepted. Use the e-file option or the mail.

sections.h2: When are Warren County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Warren County mails statements during the first week of November, and a bill is delinquent once December 31 passes. Anyone who has not received a bill by Thanksgiving should call the Collector, since a missing statement does not remove the duty to pay or the late charges.

Warren County property tax dates drawn from the Assessor and Collector pages
DateWhat happens
January 1Ownership on this day fixes who is taxed for the year
March 1Personal property lists go to the Assessor
First week of NovemberStatements are mailed
ThanksgivingCall the Collector if no bill has arrived
November 26 and 27, 2026Collector's office closed
December 24 and 25, 2026Collector's office closed
December 31Last postmark date to avoid penalty and interest

With the Thanksgiving and Christmas closures, the number of open days before the deadline is smaller than it looks. The office keeps a 24 hour drop box to the right of the entrance.

sections.h2: How does the Assessor value a house in Warren County?
sections.html:
Warren County reassesses real estate every two years, in odd-numbered years, using values as of January 1 of that year. The last full reassessment year was 2025 and the next is 2027. In even years the only changes come from new construction or demolition.

Field appraisers visit every parcel, measure any added square footage and adjust depreciation on buildings. State law sets the share of value that is taxed. A house is assessed at 19 percent of its value, farm ground at 12 percent and commercial property at 32 percent. The Assessor must also make a physical inspection before raising a home's value by more than 15 percent since the last assessment, outside of new construction.

The Assessor does not set tax rates. Schools, the county, fire districts and other taxing bodies set those, and the rate on your bill depends on which of them your address falls in.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Warren County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Notice of Change in value, which the Assessor sends when a value rises through reassessment or new construction. Compare it with what a buyer would pay for the house.

  • Ask for an informal hearing with the Assessor's staff and bring evidence of value, such as a recent sale of your property or a recent appraisal.
  • If nothing changes, make an appointment through the Assessor to be heard by the Board of Equalization, by the statutory deadline.
  • If the Board's decision still looks wrong, appeal to the State Tax Commission within 30 days after the Board's final action, or by the deadline set in the chapter if that falls later.

The Assessor's page is blunt that complaining about high taxes is not relevant testimony. The argument has to be about market value. A taxpayer who wants to pay and fight at once can file a written protest with the Collector when paying a full current bill, and must then sue in circuit court within 90 days. A taxpayer with a timely State Tax Commission appeal on file instead has the disputed part impounded.

sections.h2: What happens if tax is still owed when a Warren County house sells?
sections.html:
The owner on January 1 is the person liable for that calendar year's tax, according to the Assessor's explanation of state law. A seller who closes in March is still the person the year's bill follows under that rule, so the closing statement should say who pays it.

Ask the Collector for the amount due on the parcel before the closing date. The office accepts neither incorrect nor partial payments, and delinquent years have to be paid before the current year. Confirm the oldest year first, because anything delinquent comes ahead of the current bill.

  • Payment forms: cash, personal check, money order, cashier's check, or a card at the office or online.
  • Phone payments go through a third party at 1-877-690-3729, jurisdiction code 3563.
  • One check can cover several bills.
  • Return the bottom portion of the statement with payment.

sections.h2: Does a move out of Warren County change the vehicle tax bill?
sections.html:
No. The Assessor's site explains that personal property such as vehicles is taxed on what the owner held on January 1, even if the owner sold a car the next day or left Missouri in June. Missouri law makes no allowance for prorating the bill.

That matters for a seller who moves right after closing. The personal property statement for the year of the move still arrives, and the same December 31 postmark date applies. The Assessor adds that a taxpayer arriving in Missouri on March 1, 2026 is first assessed on January 1, 2027, and pays that bill in December 2027.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Warren County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated Warren County's population at 39,016 on July 1, 2025, up 9.8 percent from the 2020 base. Housing units totaled 17,361, and owners live in 80.2 percent of homes. The median owned home was valued at $260,400 for 2020 to 2024, the highest of Stone, Warren and Webster counties, and median gross rent was $995.

Monthly owner costs were $1,485 with a mortgage and $499 without one. Warren County issued 360 building permits in 2025, compared with 212 in Stone and 226 in Webster. About 62.8 percent of residents aged 16 and over are in the civilian labor force, and transportation and warehousing receipts reached $113.4 million in 2022.

sections.h2: Where is Warren County and which schools serve it?
sections.html:
Warren County lies on the north side of the Missouri River and is part of the St. Louis metropolitan area. It covers 438 square miles and was established on January 5, 1833. Interstate 70, U.S. Route 40, Route 47 and Route 94 cross it, and Route 94 is known as the Missouri Weinstrasse for its vineyards.

Warrenton is the county seat. Other cities are Foristell, Marthasville, Truesdale and Wright City, and the villages are Innsbrook, Pendleton and Three Creeks. Public school districts are Warren County R-III in Warrenton and Wright City R-II. Which of the two a house sits in is printed on the tax statement and changes the rate.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Warren County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Collector at 101 Mockingbird Lane, Suite 200, Warrenton, or online, by mail, by phone through the third-party line, or in the 24 hour drop box. The office phone is 636-456-3330.

faqs.q: What is the Warren County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: December 31, by postmark if mailed. Statements go out in the first week of November, and delinquent years must be paid before the current year.

faqs.q: When is the next Warren County reassessment?
faqs.a: 2027. Real estate is reassessed in odd-numbered years, and 2026 values change only for new construction or demolition.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of my Warren County tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Collector says it cannot accept incorrect or partial payments. You can pay several bills with a single check.

faqs.q: How do I dispute my Warren County valuation?
faqs.a: Ask the Assessor for an informal hearing, then an appointment with the Board of Equalization. Bring a recent sale or appraisal, since the Assessor will not consider the size of the tax bill.
